outcome: No proof, disproof, or new case resolution of the GNRS conjecture was found since 26 January 2024; the conjecture remains open in full generality and even for the long-standing open special cases of planar graphs and treewidth-3 graphs.
summary: The GNRS (planar embedding) conjecture, that every minor-closed family of graphs other than the family of all graphs has bounded-distortion embeddings into l1, remains open as of September 2026. The current Wikipedia article (fetched live, last edited 27 December 2025) still lists the conjecture as unresolved, with the only proved special cases being series-parallel/K4-minor-free graphs, O(1)-outerplanar graphs, bounded-pathwidth graphs, and 2-clique-sums of bounded-size graphs -- all results that predate the 26 January 2024 frozen revision (Lee-Sidiropoulos 2013, Lee-Poore 2013, Chekuri et al. 2006, Gupta-Newman-Rabinovich-Sinclair's own original partial results). No arXiv preprint, conference paper, or announcement in the 26 January 2024-September 2026 window claims to prove, disprove, or settle a new nontrivial case of the conjecture itself. Several adjacent papers surfaced in search but were checked and ruled out as variants rather than cases of GNRS: (1) Chang et al., 'Embedding Planar Graphs into Graphs of Treewidth O(log^3 n)' (arXiv:2411.00216, 2024-2025) addresses a different conjecture -- embedding planar graphs with (1+epsilon)-distortion into bounded-treewidth graphs, not l1 embeddings with O(1) distortion; confirmed via WebFetch that the paper explicitly treats this as a distinct problem. (2) 'Improved Lower Bounds on Multiflow-Multicut Gaps' (arXiv:2507.06576, 2025) improves a flow-cut gap lower bound for cactus graphs (a subclass of planar graphs) from 2 to 16/7, but this is a lower bound on a related but different quantity (the multiflow-multicut gap, which is bounded above by results implying GNRS-type embeddings but is not itself the l1-distortion constant), and the paper does not claim to move GNRS's own bound; it neither resolves a case of GNRS nor changes what would be written in this bullet. (3) Filtser's 'A face cover perspective to l1 embeddings of planar graphs' appeared in its journal form in ACM Transactions on Algorithms in 2025, but this is a journal publication of a SODA 2020 preprint (arXiv:1903.02758) -- the underlying result predates the window, and in any case only bounds distortion for planar metrics with bounded face-cover number, not full planar graphs, so it does not settle the planar case of GNRS either before or after the frozen date. No AI system was found associated with any of this work; none of the papers reviewed mention any AI/LLM involvement, and a targeted search for AI-related claims about GNRS turned up nothing.
competing_reading: None of the adjacent papers found are close enough calls to warrant a different classification; each addresses a demonstrably different mathematical question (bounded-treewidth stochastic embeddings, or multiflow-multicut gap lower bounds for a graph subclass) rather than restricting the GNRS statement itself. The one item worth flagging as a genuine boundary case is the Filtser ACM ToA 2025 publication: if a reader were to treat any 2025-dated appearance of a result as a 'change,' they might mark this as `progress`, but the mathematical content (face-cover-based distortion bounds) was already public via the 2020 SODA paper and 2019 arXiv preprint, so by the rule of dating to the first public written argument this is `open_stale` at most for that narrow sub-result, not a new development in the window, and it does not resolve a stated case of GNRS as posed (it bounds a parameter-dependent quantity, not distortion for all planar graphs).
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement that either (a) proves bounded l1-distortion embeddings exist for all planar graphs or all treewidth-3 graphs (long-open special cases), (b) exhibits a minor-closed family requiring unbounded distortion (a disproof), or (c) proves the general conjecture for all minor-closed families. Absent that, checking the current arXiv listings under math.MG and cs.DS for 'GNRS conjecture' or 'planar embedding conjecture' periodically would catch any future development.
